messages.subject: missing data in sleeplog
parts:
We have 14 days of actigraphy and sleeplog with some missing data. When I 
create the sleeplog I used NA for missing data. Is this acceptable for GGIR ? 

When I use the code below, it says 
" Error in matrix(0, (nrow(S) * nnights), 3) :  invalid 'nrow' value (too large or NA)" 
            #-------------------------------
             # Part 4:
             # （Labels detected sustained inactivity periods by g.part3 as either nocturnal sleep or daytime sustained inactivity) 
             #-------------------------------
             excludefirstlast = FALSE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= "~/Desktop/sleeplog_final02202018_wide.csv",
             outliers.only = FALSE,
             criterror = 0,
             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             sleeplogidnum = FALSE,
             colid=1,
             coln1=2,
             do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = c(),  


Any ideas? 
Best,
Xueping

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: missing data in sleeplog
parts:
Try by removing NAs. Also, note that you are asking for 16 hours of valid data during sleeping hours to consider a night (argument "includenightcrit = 16"). This is very unlikely, reduce this criteria as well.

Best,
Jairo

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: missing data in sleeplog
parts:
Same response as to the other question a few minutes ago:
No, this advise is incorrect. The window is defined from noon to noon, so 16 hours allows for 8 hours of nonwear time in a day, which I think is already high. I would nog advise lowering the 16 if your interest lies in sleep variables. 16 was inspired by traditional literature where 2/3 of the instructed wear duration should reflect useful data (10 out of 15 hours). Considering that modern studies have a 24 hour protocol the equivalent criteria then becomes 16 hours of required wear time per day. I think this is too soft, but I set it as a default to at least make sure users do not stick to the even worse 10 hours in the literature that had a daytime only wear protocol.
Best, Vincent

- Leave missing values blank
- See this message for an example csv file: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/RpackageGGIR/RIQyCi9ZmhA/vwU9Zc1XBAAJ
- Fill in nnights tobe the number of nights you maximally have in the sleep log for a single individual
- Check that the file is truly comma separated and not ; or , separated.
